newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South Africa faces trucking strike - paper.
newsitem.headline: South Africa faces trucking strike - paper.

text.p: Early results from a strike ballot by South Africa's Transport and General Workers' Union show overwhelming support for a strike against members of the Road Freight Employers' Association, Business Report said on Friday.

The paper quoted union national organiser Thulani Dlamini saying that after five ballot days the union's Eastern Cape, South, North and West Transvaal and South Natal branches had voted for industrial action.
If the union's 36,000 members decide to strike in the week beginning November 18, virtually all sectors of the economy would be affected.
Talks on wage increases for next year reached deadlock in September with workers demanding an across-the-board increases of between 15 and 20 percent. Employers have offered nine percent.
Dlamini said industrial action, which could combine strikes, overtime bans and work to rule, would start in the week beginning November 18.
